title: app.bin — a 2MB arm64 Mach-O executable — is committed at the head commit and not gitignored
evidence: chunk-6 diff: `diff --git a/app.bin b/app.bin` / `new file mode 100755` / `Binary files /dev/null and b/app.bin differ`. `ls -la app.bin` → `-rwxr-xr-x@ 1 moses staff 2057480 9 Aug 15:47 app.bin`; `file app.bin` → `app.bin: Mach-O 64-bit executable arm64`. `git log --oneline -1 -- app.bin` → `0118cc0 fix: pipe hit-testing follows the rendered bezier; router right-click inspects; readable HUD font` (the reviewed head). .gitignore adds only `tools/raylib-sw/`, `bin/`, `goldens/_reports/` — `grep -n "app.bin" .gitignore` → `app.bin NOT in .gitignore`.
detail: A platform-specific build artifact (arm64 Mach-O, 2MB) committed at the PR head; bloats the repo, cannot run on other platforms, and will drift stale.
recommended_fix: Remove app.bin from the tree and add `app.bin` (and any root build outputs) to .gitignore; keep builds via `odin build app` only.

title: Committed review docs (edge-case-hunter.md, verification-gap.md) describe the pre-fix code; multiple blocker/warning claims are false at the reviewed sha
evidence: `git log --oneline -- _bmad-output/reviews/odin-prototype-r1/` → `0df9135 feat: the Odin early prototype (Heist 2)...` (docs added pre-fix; fixes landed in 0118cc0). Contradictions at the sha: verification-gap.md "no step runs `odin build app`" vs ci.yml `- name: Game builds (the shipped artifact compiles)` / `run: odin build app -out:"$RUNNER_TEMP/packet-plumber"`; "T2 pixel compare silently passes when the golden is undecodable or the wrong size" vs goldens.odin `if mismatch < 0 { // undecodable or dimension-drifted golden — the pixel tier must fail loudly, never pass on nothing (review r1 blocker) ... append(fails, fmt.tprintf("T2 %dms: golden corrupt or wrong size — cannot compare (re-bless deliberately)", ms)) }`; "`harness replay` verifies only a prefix of the manifest" (`total := last_tick + 120`) vs replay.odin `replayed, ok := replay_hashes(log_path, catalogs, u64(man.ticks), false, &fails)` (empirically "250 ticks verified"); "The Sim_Driver (E21 accumulator/slow-mo) has no test" vs app/run/driver_test.odin:19-43 `@(test)` (5 tests green); edge-case-hunter.md W1 "each single healthy tick resets the 200-tick grace countdown to full" vs health.odin `if h.healthy_streak >= bal.grace_refill_streak_ticks && h.grace_ticks_left < bal.grace_window_ticks { h.grace_ticks_left = min(...) }` with comment `// (the never-lose exploit, review W1)`.
detail: Every listed blocker and most warnings (T2 -1 pass, replay prefix, QoS gap-fill, grace exploit, batch staleness, driver test) were fixed in 0118cc0, but the docs shipped unchanged; a reader at the reviewed sha gets a false picture of the PR.
recommended_fix: Update both docs to the head sha (or mark them superseded with a header noting fixes landed at 0118cc0) before merge.

title: upgrade_pipe accepts a silent downgrade: no tier-direction check, delta max(0,·) = 0, no refund, no error — reachable from the shipped demo grammar
evidence: validate_command: `if t.pipe_span[ps] > tier.max_span { return .Span_Exceeds_Tier }` ... `old := cat.pipe_tiers[t.pipe_tier[ps]]` `delta := max(0, draw_cost(t.pipe_span[ps], tier.cost_per_tile) - draw_cost(t.pipe_span[ps], old.cost_per_tile))` `if delta > budget { return .Over_Budget }` `return .None` — no `to_tier > current` check; apply: `delta_cost := max(0, draw_cost(t.pipe_span[ps], tier.cost_per_tile) - draw_cost(t.pipe_span[ps], old.cost_per_tile))` `return -delta_cost, {true, 0}`. The shipped demo attempts it: `at 400ms upgrade_pipe host-router narrow -> span_exceeds_tier` (wide→narrow, rejected only because the span exceeds narrow's max_span). Parser grammar: `upgrade_pipe <a>-<b> <tier>` (demo_parse.odin:109) accepts any tier.
detail: A downgrade on a pipe whose span fits the lower tier passes validation and silently lowers the tier at zero cost, while demolish+redraw would refund the difference; a demo author gets no error.
recommended_fix: Reject `to_tier < current tier` in validate_command (e.g. return .Unknown_Tier or a new .Downgrade error), or implement refund of the tier delta for downgrades.
